name: Ortur H20 20W
tagline: Sweet-spot H20: 20W diode on Ortur's integrated H-series frame
tldr: Ortur H20 20W balances cutting ability and price on the H20 platform. Strong hobby engraver with faster frame than LM3: verify optical power, not marketing '40W class' labels on accessories.
mainObjective: Everyday engraving plus reliable light cutting on wood, leather, and dark acrylic

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: Free air pump in Ortur's bundle for this module
Larger working area than with the top module: 420 × 300 mm per Ortur
Cuts 3 mm dark acrylic and basswood up to ~8 mm in passes
cons: Manual focus: only the top H20 module has autofocus
Fills at ~16–42 mm/s in our tests: photos remain slow for an enclosed machine at this price
Out of stock on Ortur's US store in October 2026: check availability
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 20W SKU on Ortur H20. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other modules via the chips before buying.
proTips: Use air assist for cuts on the H20, lower scan speed for photo engraving. Multiple passes at moderate speed beat one aggressive pass on basswood. Compare the 40W module benchmark if you quote production times.

moduleSystem.headline: Swappable diode & IR modules
moduleSystem.description: H20 ships as a chassis with swappable 10W, 20W, or 40W diode modules and optional 2W IR heads for metal marking: verify which module is in the box.

editorialDepth.advantages: The H20 20W module is Ortur's balanced pick on the integrated H-series chassis: enough cut depth for typical hobby boxes and signs without paying for 40W optics you may not need weekly. LightBurn support and the enclosed-ish H-frame integration beat juggling LM3 open rails if desk space matters.
editorialDepth.limitations: Still a diode inside an enclosed chassis: plan extraction on smoky cut days. Thick hardwood and cast acrylic remain CO₂ territory. If production quotes rely on fast 8 mm+ cuts, open the 40W module profile before checkout.

faq.question: Does the H20 20W come with air assist?
faq.answer: Yes. Ortur's 20W listing includes a free air pump; it was $1,379 on Ortur's store in October 2026, out of stock at the time. A 20W + 2W IR version was listed at $1,988 for those who also want to mark metal.

faq.question: What does the H20 20W cut?
faq.answer: In our benchmarks a 10 × 10 cm square in 3 mm basswood takes about 9–15 min. Basswood up to about 8 mm is realistic in several passes, as is 3 mm dark acrylic. Ortur presents this module as balanced between engraving and cutting.

faq.question: H20 20W or 40W: which one should I pick?
faq.answer: The 40W adds autofocus and cuts our 3 mm square in about 6–10 min, for about $530 more on Ortur's store ($1,909 against $1,379). It also has a slightly smaller working area (410 × 275 mm against 420 × 300 mm per Ortur). The 20W stays the better balance if you engrave as much as you cut.

standoutFeatures.title: Balanced module
standoutFeatures.body: Cuts 3 mm basswood in about 9–15 min while keeping a ~0.09 × 0.10 mm spot for engraving.

standoutFeatures.title: Air pump included
standoutFeatures.body: Ortur bundles a free air pump with this module, so cutting works out of the box.

standoutFeatures.title: Full 420 × 300 mm area
standoutFeatures.body: Ortur lists a larger working area with this module than with the top 40W head.
